title: pvWarpByScalar
body:
## pvWarpByScalar

Displaces each point along a direction by ScaleFactor × its scalar value: x' = x + ScaleFactor · s · n, with n the point normal when the input has normals and UseNormal is false, otherwise the constant Normal. XYPlane uses each point's z coordinate as s and warps along z (carpet plots). Polydata, structured and unstructured grids keep their type; image and rectilinear inputs become structured grids. Use it for elevation or carpet plots of a scalar on a surface; the curated warpScalar covers the common case.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- If the surface has point normals they are used unless UseNormal is true, so Normal may appear to be ignored.
- ScaleFactor stays 1.0 unless set (ParaView's NoDefault hint), so a scalar in pascals moves points by thousands of length units; choose a factor relative to the data range.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `WarpByScalar`. Identity: `filters/WarpScalar`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the input to the filter. Accepted data: explicit-point datasets (polygonal, unstructured or structured grids) (vtkPointSet); image data (uniform rectilinear grids) (vtkImageData); rectilinear grids (vtkRectilinearGrid). The input needs at least one point-centred array with 1 component. | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkPointSet","vtkImageData","vtkRectilinearGrid"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GenerateEnclosure` | If this value is checked and the active dataset is a 2D surface, generate a water-tight enclosure containing the initial surface, the warped surface and "side walls". | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `Normal` | The values of this property specify the direction along which to warp the dataset if any normals contained in the input dataset are not being used for this purpose. (See the UseNormal property.) | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `Scalars` | This property contains the name of the scalar array by which to warp the dataset. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"maxItems":2,"minItems":2,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE","REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `ScaleFactor` | The scalar value at a given point is multiplied by the value of this property to determine the magnitude of the change vector for that point. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `UseNormal` | If point normals are present in the dataset, the value of this property toggles whether to use a single normal value (value = 1) or the normals from the dataset (value = 0). | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `XYPlane` | If the value of this property is 1, then the Z-coordinates from the input are considered to be the scalar values, and the displacement is along the Z axis. This is useful for creating carpet plots. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
